skill.displayName: Pet Drying Box Heat Stress Analysis | 宠物烘干箱内热应激预警

llm.summary: The skill’s pet-video analysis purpose is plausible, but it silently handles account identity and tokens, uses insecure default HTTP endpoints, and can steer users toward installing a payment skill.

dimensions.detail: The implementation reads OPENCLAW sender environment values and workspace data/smyx-api-key.txt, then may send the chosen value as openId, mobile, and pnaUserName; the packaged config selects dev HTTP endpoints for these requests.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No local installer, service, or startup persistence was found, but the shared HTTP handler turns a 402 response into instructions to install smyx-payment and start a recharge workflow, with remote response text appended.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill instructs agents to query cloud history directly and not ask or show identity values; --open-id and --api-key are suppressed, and the artifact does not define clear permission boundaries for network, identity, credential, or retention behavior.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill creates or reuses a default local user in a shared workspace SQLite database and stores token/openToken fields as ordinary plaintext strings without documented cleanup, encryption, or retention limits.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Remote video analysis and cloud report history fit the stated pet heat-stress use case, but silent account creation/login, API-key-named identity reuse, plaintext token persistence, and a payment-skill prompt exceed what the narrow analysis description prepares users for.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review carefully before installing. Only use this skill if you trust the Life Emergence/SMYX service with pet videos, report history, account identifiers, and billing prompts. Avoid placing real API keys in data/smyx-api-key.txt, do not use it on sensitive networks until HTTPS production endpoints are enforced, and treat any recharge or payment-skill installation prompt as a separate manual decision.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Partly accepted: identity association can support cloud report history, but the artifact shows silent phoneLogin/registration, API-key-file fallback, token handling, and local credential storage that are not sufficiently disclosed or scoped.
[LP3] unexpected: Accepted: the skill needs file and network access for video analysis, but the artifact lacks explicit permission scoping for remote endpoints, identity sources, credential handling, and local persistence.
[SQP-2] expected: Remote media upload and cloud history are expected for server-side analysis, but retention, cleanup, identity linkage, and user-visible consent are under-disclosed.
[SDI-1] expected: Historical report listing is declared in SKILL.md, so that capability is expected, but it relies on implicit identity resolution and returns report links without clear user-facing authorization or retention details.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted: persistent user records with token and openToken fields, plus generic remote mutation helpers, are broader than necessary for a pet video analysis workflow.
[SDI-4] expected: Downgraded: subprocess-based agent execution appears only in comments/stub code, and I did not find an active subprocess execution path in the reviewed runtime.
[P9] expected: Downgraded: the whitespace findings correspond to formatting/alignment in normal Python code, not hidden reviewer-evasion content.
[YR4] expected: Downgraded: the matched manifest content is a visible pet heat-stress analysis description; I did not find offensive-tool or exploit-framework instructions in that snippet.
[T01] unexpected: Accepted: a remote 402 response causes agent-visible instructions to install smyx-payment and recharge, which is a purpose-mismatched installation/payment prompt even though it does not automatically install anything.
[T05] unexpected: Accepted: the implementation can transmit environment-derived identity or data/smyx-api-key.txt content to remote services as account identifiers, including as a mobile field.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted: reusable authentication tokens are stored in plaintext SQLite columns in the workspace data area.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted: the packaged common config selects env: dev, overriding HTTPS service URLs with plaintext private-network HTTP endpoints while requests attach identity and authentication headers.
